title: Trace Elements in Abiotic and Biotic Environments
abstract: This book helps readers understand the fundamental principles and phenomena that control the transfer of trace elements. It describes the occurrence and behavior of trace elements in rocks, soil, water, air, and plants, and also discusses the anthropogenic impact to the environment. In addition, the book covers the presence of trace elements in feeds, as either contaminants or as nutritional or zootechnical additives, and their transfer across the food chain to humans. All trace elements are covered-from aluminum to zirconium-as well as rare-earth elements (actinides and lanthanides).

narrative:
Short impact summary

Trace Elements in Abiotic and Biotic Environments (2015), published by Taylor & Francis, has been cited 375 times — enough that OpenAlex puts it in the top 10% of works in its field and year. Beyond that, it has been downloaded 3,551 times.

Full narrative

Trace Elements in Abiotic and Biotic Environments by Alina Kabata-Pendias and Barbara Szteke was published by Taylor & Francis in 2015. Conceptually, the work connects to Abiotic component, TRACE (psycholinguistics), Biotic component, Environmental science and Ecology.

OpenAlex records 375 citations. That places it in the top 10% of works in its field and year of publication. Citations peaked in 2023 with 79 citing works. Notable citing venues include The Science of The Total Environment, Environmental Science and Pollution Research and Environmental Monitoring and Assessment. Of the citation statements scite has classified, 14 support its claims and 1 contradict them. The citing works include 335 journal articles, 19 book chapters and 10 preprints. They come from 40 countries, led by Poland, India and Brazil.

It has been downloaded 3,551 times via OAPEN. Open Library reports a combined count of 9 reading logs and catalog editions. Its subject matter aligns with Zero hunger among the Sustainable Development Goals.
